text:
Predicates:
Taller(x, y) ::: x is taller than y.
CanBlock(x, y) ::: x can block y's shooting.
Jumping(x) ::: x can jump when shooting.
GreatShooter(x) ::: x is a great shooter.
Michael ::: a specific individual named Michael.
Windy ::: a specific individual named Windy.
Peter ::: a specific individual named Peter.
Premises:
∀x ∀y (Taller(x, y) → CanBlock(x, y)) ::: If x is taller than y, then x can block y's shooting.
Taller(Michael, y) for all y in class ::: Michael is taller than everyone in his class.
∀x ∀y ∀z ((Taller(x, y) ∧ Taller(y, z)) → Taller(x, z)) ::: If x is taller than y and y is taller than z, then x is taller than z.
Taller(Peter, Michael) ::: Peter is taller than Michael.
¬CanBlock(Michael, Windy) ::: Michael cannot block Windy's shooting.
Jumping(x) → GreatShooter(x) ::: Any shooter who can jump is a great shooter.
Premises (additional context):
Taller(x, y) and ¬Jumping(x) imply CanBlock(x, y) ::: Michael can block anyone taller than him unless they jump.
Conclusion:
CanBlock(Peter, Windy) ::: Peter can block Windy's shooting.
